items.one_liner: Vidar Stealer utilizes custom XOR string encryption, anti-forensic DNS flushing, and browser process injection to exfiltrate session tokens filelessly.
items.summary: An analysis of a Vidar Stealer sample in Binary Ninja demonstrates heavy obfuscation, including random function names, custom XOR string encryption, and runtime memory assembly designed to bypass static antivirus signatures. The malware performs system reconnaissance and anti-forensic cleanup by resolving WinAPI calls to flush DNS caches (DnsFlushResolverCache), query network adapters (GetIfEntry), and execute deletion tasks via WinExec. It ultimately utilizes process hollowing and pipe redirection to inject its payload directly into browser memory spaces, such as chrome.exe, allowing fileless execution while targeting Google and Reddit session data.
key_facts: Key APIs: DnsFlushResolverCache, GetIfEntry, WinExec, CreatePipe
items.bottom_line: Advanced infostealers like Vidar bypass static file scanners by executing entirely in-memory and injecting payloads directly into active browser processes.

items.title: When Planning Problems Become Hard for LLMs: Separating Structural Complexity from Semantic Interpretability
items.one_liner: LLM planning failures stem more from predicate semantics than structural difficulty, proving that classical symbolic heuristics already estimate structural complexity well.
items.summary: Researchers examined seven STRIPS planning domains to distinguish structural difficulty from semantic vocabulary interpretation in LLM planning tasks. The zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic h_add outperformed learned alternatives like ridge regression, object count, and ARC for predicting structural difficulty on held-out domains with a mean Spearman |rho| of 0.931. To isolate semantic effects, the authors progressively renamed predicates while keeping states, transitions, and optimal plans identical, showing that valid LLM planning success dropped from 67.5% to 40.0% between 0% and 100% renaming. The findings indicate that symbolic heuristics already estimate structural difficulty effectively, meaning future hybrid planning improvements should focus on modeling LLM behavior sensitive to predicate semantics rather than building new structural predictors.

items.title: When LLMs Manipulate: Measuring Behavioral, Social, and Temporal Effects
items.one_liner: A new behavioral framework demonstrates that manipulative LLM framing prompts significant, measurable shifts in user compliance and trust calibration.
items.summary: Researchers introduced a behavioral computing framework to measure user susceptibility to manipulative outputs from large language models, termed behavioral vulnerability. items.title: CALLIOPE: Private Insights into AI Use, Without Embeddings
items.one_liner: CALLIOPE uses direct LLM capabilities instead of vector embeddings to extract private topic hierarchies from unstructured text.
items.summary: Researchers introduce CALLIOPE, a top-down framework for discovering topic hierarchies in unstructured text corpora such as large LLM conversations while maintaining differential privacy (DP). Unlike traditional and recent methods that rely on clustering vector embeddings, CALLIOPE directly leverages LLM capabilities for the entire pipeline. Experimental evaluations demonstrate superior utility over embedding-based approaches under differential privacy settings, particularly in high-privacy regimes.
items.bottom_line: CALLIOPE achieves superior utility over embedding-based clustering for differential privacy topic discovery in LLM conversation corpora.

items.title: Evolving Self-tuning Benchmarks for Long-Horizon Tool Use
items.one_liner: TURTLE is an unsupervised LLM agent framework that automatically generates evolving, difficult tool-use benchmarks.
items.summary: To improve AI assistant tool-use capabilities across applications like Gmail, Venmo, and Slack without relying on costly human supervision, researchers proposed TURTLE (Tool Use Related Tasks with Long-Horizon Evolution). TURTLE uses an Unsupervised Environment Design approach powered by proposer, solver, and feedback generator LLM agents to automatically evolve tasks for difficulty and diversity. Empirical evaluations across AppWorld, tau-Bench, and AutomationBench using Gemma 4 31B-it showed that the framework successfully increased hard task generation by 165% on AppWorld while broadening task diversity and failure modes.
key_facts: Benchmark Improvement: 165% increase in hard tasks on AppWorld
items.bottom_line: Automated environment design frameworks like TURTLE can effectively scale the creation of complex, long-horizon tool-use benchmarks for AI assistants.
